extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, communications officers, and journalists/media relations practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and evaluating press releases with an emphasis on credibility and trustworthiness, including general quality markers and crisis-communication rules. Useful for PR teams preparing releases and for journalists vetting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable spokesperson credentials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a named spokesperson whose professional credentials are easily verifiable (e.g., findable on LinkedIn). Journalists will check spokesperson credentials and may call the person directly to confirm quote authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology disclosed for any data claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology disclosed for any data claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any statistical or research claim should be accompanied by a clear description of methods. Avoid phrases like 'according to our internal data' without methodology. Journalists look for survey methodology, sample size, and margin of error when verifying claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding sources and conflicts of interest noted
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding sources / conflicts of interest noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose who funded the research or release and any relevant conflicts. 'Independent' sources that have hidden funding are treated with suspicion; transparent funding disclosures build credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verifiable third-party confirmations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with confirmable third-party evidence (e.g., customer or partner confirmations). Journalists will seek customer/partner confirmations as part of verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct phone number for follow-up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a phone number journalists can use to reach a real person; this facilitates quick verification and builds trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with public records
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure numerical and factual claims align with public records. Journalists will check numbers against public records such as SEC filings and other official sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague research claims without links
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague 'leading research' claims with no link to actual study are suspicious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If referencing research, link to the study or provide citation details. Vague claims without sources are treated as PR spam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unverifiable or fake spokespeople/quotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes from spokespeople you can't find on LinkedIn are a red flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real, verifiable spokespeople and be prepared for journalists to call and confirm the person actually said the quoted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not claim 'internal data' without methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: 'According to our internal data' without methodology is suspicious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either provide the methodology or avoid citing opaque internal metrics. Journalists will discount claims that cannot be independently assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes require clear reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Embargo with no clear reason for delay is suspicious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issuing an embargo, state the reason and be reliable about it; repeated embargo violations erode trust between sources and reporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report survey margin of error and sample details
rubrics_metrics.description: Surveys with no margin of error reported are problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include survey methodology, sample size, and margin of error. Journalists will verify survey methodology and sample size when assessing credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'independent' sources with hidden funding
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Independent' sources with hidden funding are suspect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If citing independent experts or organizations, disclose funding relationships that could introduce bias; undisclosed funding undermines the independence claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apology must come before explanation (crisis rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apology must come before explanation in crisis press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When addressing a crisis, lead with an apology before explaining circumstances. This sequencing is critical to perceived sincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize specifics over statements of values in crises
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifics matter more than statements of values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In crisis communications, provide concrete facts and actions rather than abstract statements about values; journalists and the public expect specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a timeline of what was known and when
rubrics_metrics.description: Timeline of what was known and when.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail the chronology of events to show transparency about when information became available and what steps were taken at each point.

rubrics_metrics.name: List specific corrective actions (not abstract commitments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific corrective actions in crisis releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail measurable, concrete corrective steps instead of vague promises. Specificity increases accountability and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name the harm; do not deflect
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify who was harmed and how, rather than minimizing or deflecting blame. Avoid phrasing like 'regret that some may have felt' which sidesteps responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists will verify quotes by calling sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for reporters to call quoted individuals to confirm what was said; inaccurate or fabricated quotes will be exposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial claims should be verifiable against filings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure financial assertions match official filings (e.g., SEC). Journalists will cross-check monetary claims with public financial documents.
